item.description:
**The menus offer only what works.** With the SFTP window or Settings in front, New Host…, New Group…, New Local Shell, Import… and Quick Connect… were enabled and did nothing, and so was Shellhand ▸ SFTP with nothing to open it from. Reconnect was live on a local shell, which has no host to reconnect to. They grey out now. macOS's own window tabs are gone from View and Window, where they offered a tab bar and a second pair of tab items on the strip's own keys. And two tabs on the same host each get a ⌘ number of their own in the Window menu — "refuser" and "refuser (2)" — where both landed on one.
**Deleting a group says what really happens.** It said all of a group's hosts moved to the top of the list, when only the ones filed in it directly do: the groups inside it move up with their own hosts still in them. It says so now, and says that what the group gives those hosts — the user, the key, the palette — goes with it.
**The palette picker fits in Settings.** It was taller than the Settings window, which left its Done button below the window's edge. It now fits the window it opens over.
**The SFTP window opens with the keyboard in This Mac's list**, as the host window opens in its host list, rather than in the path field, where ↓, Space and ⌫ edited the path.
**The host editor speaks like the rest of the app.** Its inherited values say "from Production", as the group editor and the inspector do, and the settings it called Through and Agent are Jump host and Agent forwarding, as they are everywhere else.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 753 checks to 756.

**⌘W closes the tab again, not the window.** Since 0.1.3, ⌘W went to the system's own Close rather than Shellhand's Close Tab, so it closed the whole window. With a session still running it asked about the window; with nothing running it closed the window and every tab in it without a word. ⌘W closes the tab in front again, asking first while its session is still running, and closes SFTP or Settings when one of them is in front.
**A session that is still connecting says so.** A warning ssh prints before it reaches the host — a key file that is not there is the usual one — made the session read as connected: its tab went green and Stop Connecting greyed out while ssh was still trying. Those warnings no longer count as the host answering, so the session stays connecting, with its time and Stop Connecting, until something does.
**Show Beside fits the window.** Showing a tab beside the one in front widened the window past the edge of the screen, cutting off the right-hand side and pushing the inspector out of reach. The two sides now share the width the window has, half each to begin with, and the line between them can be dragged.
**An import leaves your hosts where you filed them.** The group typed into "Put new hosts in" was given to every host the file left unfiled, including ones already in your list, so importing your ssh config a second time with a group typed moved hosts out of the groups you had put them in. It now files only the hosts the import adds.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 746 checks to 753. A walk through the whole window after 0.1.4 found all four of these, and the window check now fails if ⌘W belongs to anything but Close Tab.

**Renaming a host takes what goes through it along.** A host that others jumped through, named in their Through field or in a group's, left them naming a machine no longer in the list once it was renamed, and ssh was left to find one by that name on its own. Saving a new name now rewrites every host's and group's Through field that named the old one, and the editor says what will follow before you save — "6 hosts and the groups EU and US go through bastion, and will follow the new name."
**The window opens with the keyboard in the host list.** macOS gave it to the search field, the window's first text field, so ↓ and Return did nothing until the list was clicked. Now the arrows walk the list and Return connects from the moment the window opens. ⌘F still goes to the search.
**A host called bastion is no longer offered itself to jump through.** The Through field's grey example was "bastion" on every host, which on a host called bastion read as the loop Shellhand refuses to save. There it suggests "gateway" instead.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 737 checks to 746, and the README's picture and shellhand.com show the window as it is now, where they showed an older one.
